correctness.rationale: Let D be (1,2)-dominating and R its complement. Cubicity gives |E(D,R)|<=|D| because every D-vertex has at most one crossing neighbor, while domination gives |E(D,R)|>=|R| because every R-vertex has at least one crossing neighbor. Thus |D|>=n/2. Equality forces crossing degree exactly one at every vertex, hence a perfect matching cut; conversely a perfect matching cut leaves internal degree two on each shore, making either shore a (1,2)-dominating set of size n/2. All quantifiers and both directions are explicit.
